source.title: ZiCo: Zero-shot NAS via Inverse Coefficient of Variation on Gradients
source.authors: Gui-Hong Li; Yue-Dong Yang; K. Bhardwaj; R. Marculescu

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendices; no relevant truncation is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports theoretical and empirical results about gradient properties and training convergence, using regression loss on MNIST rather than the classification error and settings named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The MNIST loss results bear on gradient properties and convergence, but do not measure whether the classification networks in V1–V6 reach near-zero training error. The NAS proxy correlations, architecture search outcomes, and cited prior findings do not test those versions.
record.test_reason: The study tests relationships between gradient statistics and MNIST regression loss, then evaluates an architecture-ranking proxy. None of its own results tests V1–V6: it does not measure near-zero classification training error, spurious minima versus extra width, depth degradation and shortcuts, initialization comparisons, stability-threshold dynamics, or normalization effects. Using Kaiming initialization as a fixed recipe does not test V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the authors' interpretation, but omits generalization and the main NAS conclusion. The authors argue that larger absolute gradient means and smaller gradient standard deviations favor convergence and generalization, motivate ZiCo from these properties, and report competitive architecture-ranking and search performance at low search cost. The empirical loss plots establish associations after an update or epoch; they do not independently establish causal effects on convergence speed.
record.recipe_differences: The empirical convergence experiments use MNIST regression losses and gradient-property comparisons, rather than the claim versions' classification-error experiments and settings. The paper also evaluates a zero-shot architecture-ranking proxy.
record.method_sensitivity: For the MLP loss comparisons, the stated batch size is 256 in the main result and 64, 128, and 256 in the supplementary experiment; learning rate is η = 10⁻⁸. The paper also reports that ZiCo correlation varies with the number of batches and batch size, but those proxy correlations do not measure the claim's training-error outcome.

fits_no_version.finding: In the MNIST linear regression experiments, higher squared gradient means and lower summed gradient variances accompany lower post-update training loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Across the studied linear-model runs, gradient mean and variance are associated with post-update regression loss.

fits_no_version.finding: Two-layer ReLU MLPs with lower gradient standard deviation across batches tend to have lower training and test MSE after one epoch on MNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the studied MNIST regression setup, gradient variability is associated with one-epoch training and test loss.

record.problems: The convergence results are qualitative trends from figures, with no reported uncertainty estimates or stated controls. They use MNIST regression and do not establish near-zero classification training error in the claim's settings.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported results meet the row criteria for the claim versions. NAS proxy correlations and architecture test accuracies concern proxy ranking or downstream performance, not the versions' training-error outcomes; comparisons cited from prior work were not extracted as this study's results.

untested.parts: Near-zero CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training classification error, including random or corrupted labels and dependence on size, stopping, and regularization.
Teacher–student spurious local minima and their reduction with one or two extra student neurons.
Training degradation with depth, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization exceptions.
Effects of initialization choices on signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Recovery or divergence relative to stability limits, transient loss increases, curvature reduction, and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V6, not denials of the reported qualitative associations. Supplementary batch-size results and NAS evaluations are already declared in rows_left_out or elsewhere in the record and add no test of these versions.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, network size, optimizer, or training duration.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student local-minima experiment or width comparison.
No initialization comparison or trainable-depth experiment; Kaiming initialization is stated for the NAS search space but not varied.
No learning-rate stability-limit or sharpness experiment.

rows.subject: linear model as in Eq. 2
rows.stage_stated: randomly sampled network instances; initialization not stated
rows.operation_detail: Updated parameters using accumulated gradients on 1,000 normalized MNIST training images with learning rate η = 1; plotted training loss against square sum of mean gradients.
rows.measure: Total training loss versus square sum of mean gradients
rows.value: Networks with higher square sum of mean gradients tend to have lower training loss.
rows.note: Qualitative trend stated in the text; the figure does not provide tabulated values.
rows.check: The qualitative loss association is reported correctly, but it cannot establish any claim version. The text states 1,000 repetitions on the same dataset; it does not explicitly establish that these are randomly sampled network instances. Section 4.2 describes an accumulated-gradient update, while Figure 1's caption calls the duration one epoch.

rows.subject: linear model as in Eq. 2
rows.stage_stated: randomly sampled network instances; initialization not stated
rows.operation_detail: Updated parameters using accumulated gradients on 1,000 normalized MNIST training images with learning rate η = 1; plotted training loss against square sum of gradient variances.
rows.measure: Total training loss versus square sum of gradient variances
rows.value: Networks with a lower square sum of variance tend to have lower training loss.
rows.note: Qualitative trend stated in the text; the figure does not provide tabulated values.
rows.check: The qualitative variance–loss association is reported correctly but measures no claim version. Random sampling of network instances is not explicitly stated. The variance bound in Eq. 6 assumes η = 1/M, whereas Section 4.2 reports η = 1 with M = 1,000; the empirical association should not be presented as a matched-condition validation of that bound.

rows.subject: two-layer MLP with ReLU as defined in Eq. 7
rows.operation_detail: Applied gradient descent for one epoch on MNIST and compared training loss with gradient standard deviation across batches.
rows.measure: Training loss versus standard deviation of gradients across batches
rows.value: Networks with lower gradient standard deviation tend to have lower training loss values.
rows.note: The text reports a tendency, not exact plotted values.
rows.check: Lower one-epoch MSE associated with lower gradient standard deviation does not measure any claim version. Eq. 7's theoretical setup fixes the second-layer weights and optimizes the first layer; this qualification should accompany the model description. The reported trend alone does not establish a convergence-rate comparison.

rows.subject: two-layer MLP with ReLU as defined in Eq. 7
rows.operation_detail: Applied gradient descent for one epoch on MNIST and compared test loss with gradient standard deviation across batches.
rows.measure: Test loss versus standard deviation of gradients across batches
rows.value: Networks with lower gradient standard deviation tend to have lower test loss values.
rows.note: The text reports a tendency, not exact plotted values.
rows.check: Test MSE versus gradient standard deviation measures generalization performance rather than any version's optimization effect. Figure 2(b) is the correct test-loss panel despite the prose's repeated reference to Figure 2(a). The qualitative association is accurately extracted.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
